name: Radar-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The bright sweep beam is angled across the rings with the full spoke pattern visible.

tagline: A purple radar sweep turns over rings and spokes on black.
summary: A radar display in violet on black, built from even concentric rings and straight spokes converging on a bright hub. A brighter beam rotates around it, lighting the rings as it passes.
appearance: A circular instrument centred on a black stage, drawn with a few thin lavender rings and about a dozen radial spokes. The centre is a small dark hole ringed by a hot violet glow, and the edges fade into black.
behaviour: One brighter wedge sweeps around the dial at a steady speed, and the rings pulse gently outward from the hub. Moving the pointer slides the whole display a little and it eases back on leave.
use_when: A monitoring, security or analytics page wants a radar motif behind or beside its data.
avoid_when: You need accurate data display: it is a decorative sweep with no real plotting.
customise: Ring and spoke counts and thickness, sweep speed, width and lobes, colours, falloff, brightness and pointer influence are all props.
weight_why: A full-screen shader runs per-pixel ring, spoke and sweep maths every frame.

a11y.note: Decorative and always sweeping, with no reduced-motion check and no keyboard path.

issues: The sweep and hub blow out to white, hiding the violet at the centre.
polish_why: Crisp, well-proportioned radar with a convincing sweep; the core clips bright.
